analyst_view.overall: Sporting (12th, 9 points, five wins in a row in all competitions) host Manchester United (19th, 6 points); a win would put Sporting near the top eight, while United need points to stay in the play-off spots. Both have new coaches: Paulo Fonseca at Sporting, who said United are hard to read and expects to spend spells in a mid-to-low block and counter-attack, and Mauricio Pochettino at United, whose first game was a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool. United are without Matheus Cunha (one-match UEFA ban for his red card against Roma, confirmed by ESPN and others), whom the numbers don't list, plus Sesko, Ugarte, Baleba and Rashford (counted); Shaw travelled but is a doubt, while Maguire is fit and expected to start, with Fernandes behind Zirkzee or Mount. Sporting are without Debast and Nuno Santos (counted) but have Ioannidis and Flavio back; Polish referee Szymon Marciniak (about 3.5 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals (1.7 Sporting, 1.1 United), already taking Sesko off United. Cunha's ban is not on their list and removes one of United's main creators and scorers, and Fonseca planning to sit deeper at times against a side under a brand-new coach points to a cagier game, so I lean a little lower, to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, fairly even (4.3 Sporting, 5.0 United). Sporting's low-block spells could give United more corners and Sporting fewer, which roughly cancels out, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already taking about 9% off for Marciniak's record and 11% for Sporting's calm recent run, and adding a little for United's busier one. Both coaches expect a tense game but nothing in the news points to a rougher one than the records suggest, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.0 shots, lifted for both sides' recent shooting. Without Cunha United lose a player who shoots a lot from outside the box, and Sporting will defend deeper at times and look to counter, so I trim to about 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target, split evenly. Losing Cunha takes some quality out of United's attack and Shaw is a doubt on the left, while Sporting's side is close to full strength, so I trim to about 10.1.
